reference.source: ILAE classification / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Caused by variants in SLC2A1 encoding the GLUT1 glucose transporter, impairing glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier
Early-onset epilepsy, often in infancy, is common and may include absence, myoclonic, generalised tonic-clonic or focal seizures
The clinical picture combines seizures with developmental delay, acquired microcephaly and a complex movement disorder including ataxia and dystonia
Symptoms characteristically fluctuate and may worsen with fasting or exertion and improve after eating
A paroxysmal exercise-induced dyskinesia phenotype and early-onset absence epilepsy are recognised presentations
The ketogenic diet is the specific and highly effective treatment, providing ketones as an alternative cerebral fuel
Prompt recognition matters because early dietary treatment can improve seizures, movement and cognitive outcomes
reference.pathophysiology: GLUT1 deficiency syndrome results from variants in SLC2A1 encoding the GLUT1 transporter responsible for facilitated glucose entry across the blood-brain barrier and into astrocytes. Reduced transporter function causes a chronic shortfall of glucose in the brain despite normal blood glucose, so cerebral energy supply becomes inadequate, particularly at times of increased demand such as fasting or exertion. This energy deficit produces seizures, movement disorder and impaired brain development, and it is bypassed therapeutically by providing ketone bodies through the ketogenic diet as an alternative fuel.
additionalDifferentials: Childhood and early-onset absence epilepsy of other cause
Primary movement disorders with paroxysmal dyskinesia
additionalInvestigations: Lumbar puncture showing a low CSF glucose with a low CSF-to-blood glucose ratio in the fasting state, with normal blood glucose
SLC2A1 gene testing to confirm the diagnosis
EEG, which may show generalised or focal discharges and can improve after eating
Brain MRI, usually unremarkable or non-specific, to exclude other pathology
Assessment of development, movement and head growth over time
redFlags: Early-onset epilepsy with a movement disorder and acquired microcephaly
Seizures or symptoms that clearly worsen with fasting and improve with food
Low CSF glucose with normal blood glucose
Paroxysmal exercise-induced dyskinesia with cognitive or seizure involvement
reference.prognosis: With early institution of the ketogenic diet, seizure control and movement symptoms often improve substantially, though some cognitive and motor impairment may persist. Delayed diagnosis and treatment are associated with worse neurodevelopmental outcomes.
pitfalls: Measuring CSF glucose without a paired fasting blood glucose, obscuring the diagnostic ratio
Attributing early-onset absence or myoclonic epilepsy solely to a common genetic generalised epilepsy
Overlooking the fasting-dependent fluctuation of symptoms
Failing to consider the ketogenic diet as specific, effective treatment
